This file checks the data before we commit to it (see the checklist on the
course page "Finding Data for Your Project"). Run `R/01_get_data.R` first.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)

# Quarto runs this file from analysis/, so go up one level to the project root
spotify <- read_csv(here::here("data", "spotify_clean.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## 1. Are the variables there, and how many observations?

```{r}
#| label: size
nrow(spotify)
glimpse(spotify)

# Missing values per column
spotify |> summarise(across(everything(), \(x) sum(is.na(x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "n_missing") |>
  filter(n_missing > 0)
```

## 2. Outcome: Spotify popularity (Y)

```{r}
#| label: popularity
spotify |>
  summarise(mean = mean(track_popularity), median = median(track_popularity),
            sd = sd(track_popularity), share_zero = mean(zero_pop))

ggplot(spotify, aes(track_popularity)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2) +
  labs(x = "Spotify popularity (0-100)", y = "Number of songs")
```

About 9% of songs have popularity 0. Many are older or duplicate versions of a
song. We will compare results with and without them.

## 3. Popularity by genre and release year

```{r}
#| label: by-genre
spotify |>
  group_by(genre) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean_pop = mean(track_popularity)) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_pop))

ggplot(spotify, aes(reorder(genre, track_popularity), track_popularity)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Genre", y = "Spotify popularity")
```

```{r}
#| label: by-year
spotify |>
  filter(release_year >= 1970) |>
  group_by(release_year) |>
  summarise(mean_pop = mean(track_popularity), n = n()) |>
  ggplot(aes(release_year, mean_pop)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Album release year", y = "Mean popularity")
```

## 4. Explanatory variables: audio features (X)

```{r}
#| label: features
features <- c("danceability", "energy", "loudness", "speechiness", "acousticness",
              "instrumentalness", "liveness", "valence", "tempo", "duration_min")

# Correlation of each audio feature with popularity
spotify |>
  summarise(across(all_of(features), \(x) cor(x, track_popularity))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "feature", values_to = "cor_with_popularity") |>
  arrange(desc(abs(cor_with_popularity)))

spotify |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(features), names_to = "feature", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(value, track_popularity)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.03) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ feature, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Spotify popularity")
```

## 5. A first regression (baseline only)

```{r}
#| label: baseline-lm
m0 <- lm(track_popularity ~ genre + release_year, data = spotify)
m1 <- lm(track_popularity ~ genre + release_year + danceability + energy + loudness +
           speechiness + acousticness + instrumentalness + liveness + valence +
           tempo + duration_min + mode, data = spotify)

summary(m1)

# How much do audio features add beyond genre and year?
c(r2_genre_year = summary(m0)$r.squared, r2_with_audio = summary(m1)$r.squared)
```
